ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.AllEnemies)` (Breakthrough.cs:19-22) == cost 1 / ATTACK / COMMON / ALL_ENEMIES. `handles_own_routing = True` (breakthrough.py:31) is faithful, not an addition: C#'s OnPlay runs ONCE and `TargetingAllOpponents` fans out inside the attack command, whereas the sim's framework would call `on_play` once per living enemy (combat.py:481-487) and repeat the one-shot self-damage.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: _damage = 9 declared; the 1 HP loss is inlined (breakthrough.py:34, 44)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new DamageVar(9m, ValueProp.Move)` maps to `_damage = 9`, but `new HpLossVar(1m)` (Breakthrough.cs:13-17) has no `_hp_loss` in `_init_vars`, so `Card.base_hp_loss` reports 0. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no corresponding `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. DORMANT for game fidelity (the dealt number is identical), LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.issue: The AoE half is faithful (`DamageCmd.Attack(9).FromCard(this).TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)`, Breakthrough.cs:28-30, == a per-enemy `DamageCmd.deal(..., dealer=ctx.player, card=self)`), and so is the order (self-damage FIRST). THE SELF-DAMAGE BYPASSES THE DAMAGE PIPELINE ENTIRELY. C# calls `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.HpLoss.BaseValue, Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, this)` (Breakthrough.cs:27) -- the full pipeline: the damage modifiers, the damage cap, `Hook.AfterCurrentHpChanged`, `Hook.AfterDamageReceived`, the death check and Kill. The sim hand-rolls it: `p.hp = max(0, p.hp - 1)` plus a bare `on_hp_changed` and a manual `should_die`/`on_death` (breakthrough.py:42-50), so `on_damage_received` never fires and no damage modifier is consulted. Observable through RupturePower, which gains Strength on any unblocked damage its owner receives (`RupturePower.AfterDamageReceived`, RupturePower.cs:44-57 -- with cardSource null the immediate-apply branch at line 48 is taken) and whose sim port listens on `on_damage_received` (powers.py:272-289). Play Breakthrough holding Rupture: the game gains Strength, the sim does not. LIVE -- card/rupture is a ported Ironclad card (sts2_rl/cards/rupture_card.py) and Breakthrough is a ported Common. The bypass also skips the Intangible cap and Buffer, which would matter for any larger card-sourced HP loss. Presentation, folded in: VfxCmd.PlayOnCreatureCenter (26) and WithHitFx (29).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(4m)` (Breakthrough.cs:35) == `self._damage += 4` (9 -> 13). The 1 HP loss is unchanged by the upgrade on both sides.

guards.what: the enemy loop skips on `enemy.is_dead`, not `enemy.is_gone` (breakthrough.py:54)
guards.issue: Every other AoE card in the sim filters on `not e.is_gone` (conflagration, shockwave, omnislice, sword_boomerang, rip_and_tear -- see `py tools/audit/card_probes.py dead-target-guards`), and `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Breakthrough alone uses `is_dead`, so an ESCAPED-but-alive enemy is still struck. C#'s `TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` resolves against the combat's live opponent list, from which an escaped creature has been removed (`CreatureCmd.Escape`, CreatureCmd.cs:579-603). DORMANT: no ported Ironclad-reachable monster escapes while a second enemy is still alive to keep the combat running, so the extra target is never reached today; live with any ported escaping monster in a multi-enemy fight.

guards.what: the per-enemy `if ctx.player.is_dead: break` inside the AoE loop (breakthrough.py:55-56)
guards.rationale: Mirrors the combat-over check the game's attack command performs between hits; both stop fanning out once the player has died mid-attack (thorns, Flame Barrier).
